paper_metadata.title: Quantum optimisation via maximally amplified states

summary: The paper introduces the Maximum Amplification Optimisation Algorithm (MAOA), a Grover-based near-term optimization method, and evaluates it only in numerical simulation on two problems: a 10-location capacitated vehicle routing problem and a 20-stock portfolio optimization problem. In both cases, MAOA outperforms restricted Grover adaptive search and classical random sampling in simulation, with the paper deriving an asymptotic speedup of 2r+1 over classical random sampling in the small-target-ratio limit; no physical quantum hardware results are reported.

experiments.description: Maximum Amplification Optimisation Algorithm (MAOA) and restricted Grover adaptive search (RGAS) simulated on a capacitated vehicle routing problem with 10 locations; compared against unrestricted Grover adaptive search and classical random sampling.

algorithm.variant: MAOA; RGAS; Grover adaptive search benchmark
algorithm.optimizer: Nelder-Mead (for threshold/parameter search in MAOA and benchmark optimization runs)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: For MAOA threshold-finding: 20 consecutive successful measurements at a threshold to accept a peak; for adaptive search: 40 consecutive successful measurements at the final threshold
algorithm.parameter_initialization: MAOA: initial threshold near median estimated from 200 sampled solutions; initial step size from quartile spread; benchmark optimization uses 10,000 random parameter sets and Nelder-Mead refinement

optimizer_settings.step_size: adaptive threshold step size derived from interquartile range and previous peak spacings

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each solution corresponds to a route assignment in the combinatorial solution space; binary marking function used to mark solutions below a cost threshold
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Feasibility handled by the problem definition and solution-space indexing; binary threshold marking on cost

problem_instance.description: Capacitated vehicle routing problem with 10 locations and a randomly generated cost structure
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Package vector randomly generated from integers in [5,30]; symmetric cost matrix with depot-to-location costs in [10,20] and inter-location costs in [1,15]; vehicle capacity set to 20
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10,000 simulations; success probability vs computational effort curves; success defined as measuring one of the 12 lowest-cost solutions

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Precomputed solution-quality distribution for the CVRP instance
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Select best solution among measured samples; compute success probability curves

results.unit: x (relative to classical random sampling in the small-target-ratio limit, asymptotically 2r+1)

speedup_claims.conditions: small target-ratio limit; repeated preparation and measurement of the maximally amplified state; per-sample cost counted as 2r+1
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this is the asymptotic speedup in the small-target-ratio limit; actual empirical curves depend on the chosen rotation count and threshold-finding overhead.

speedup_claims.factor: MAOA outperforms RGAS and both outperform classical random sampling
speedup_claims.baseline_method: restricted Grover adaptive search and classical random sampling
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide a single numeric speedup factor from the plotted curves in text.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(sqrt(N)) for unrestricted Grover adaptive search; MAOA uses r Grover rotations with per-sample cost O(2r+1)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N) for random sampling / exhaustive-style baseline
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Speedup over classical random sampling tends to 2r+1 in the small-target-ratio limit

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not reported; the paper gives asymptotic speedup e_C/e_Q -> 2r+1 for small target ratios, but no hardware crossover size.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Restricted Grover rotations with per-sample cost 2r+1; tested at r = 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, with unrestricted GAS benchmark requiring r_max = 6029.
limiting_factors: Speedup is relative to random sampling, not best classical CVRP heuristics
Performance depends on threshold-finding and repeated state preparation

notes: No physical QPU is named; experiments are numerical simulations, so hardware.type inferred as simulator_other.
The paper reports rotation counts r rather than qubit register size; num_qubits is not explicitly stated and remains null.

Speedup order inferred from the paper's derived asymptotic result e_C/e_Q -> 2r+1, i.e. linear in circuit depth, which is a polynomial_other speedup rather than an asymptotic quantum advantage over classical exhaustive search.
The paper reports only numerical simulations and an asymptotic comparison to classical random sampling.
It does not demonstrate a practical quantum advantage on hardware.

experiments.description: MAOA and RGAS simulated on a portfolio optimization problem with 20 ASX stocks and a fixed net position constraint; compared against unrestricted Grover adaptive search and classical random sampling.

algorithm.variant: MAOA; RGAS; Grover adaptive search benchmark
algorithm.optimizer: Nelder-Mead (for threshold/parameter search in MAOA and benchmark optimization runs)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio choices encoded as ternary vectors z_i in {-1,0,1}; the MAOA uses a binary threshold on return after fixing a risk threshold
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize expected return subject to a low-risk filter; return = sum_i R_i z_i, risk = sum_{i,j} sigma_ij z_i z_j
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Two-threshold marking: risk threshold fixed to the lowest 10% of solutions, then return threshold optimized within that subspace

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization over 20 ASX stocks with daily adjusted close prices from 2019-01-01 to 2020-12-31

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Daily adjusted close prices used to compute expected returns and covariance matrix

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Daily adjusted close prices analyzed to estimate daily expected percentage returns and covariance matrix; risk values scaled down by factor 100 in the figure
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10,000 simulations; success probability vs computational effort; success defined as finding the single highest-return portfolio within the lowest 10% risk subset

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Precomputed solution-quality distribution from market data; fixed risk threshold to reduce the 2D problem to 1D
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Select best portfolio among measured samples; compute success probability curves

speedup_claims.conditions: 20-stock ASX portfolio; low-risk subset fixed to lowest 10%; r in {32,64,128,256,512}; 10,000 simulations

experiments.description: MAOA and RGAS simulated on an arbitrarily large normally distributed solution space, using a standard normal quality distribution and varying target ratios; compared against classical random sampling.

algorithm.variant: MAOA; RGAS; Grover adaptive search benchmark
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Fixed rotation count r = 64; MAOA uses a threshold in the low-convergence regime where P(r, rho(T)) <= 1/40
algorithm.parameter_initialization: MAOA threshold chosen via threshold-response navigation; RGAS uses randomized rotation counts with upper bound growth parameter lambda

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Abstract large solution space with solutions distributed according to a standard normal quality distribution; marked set defined by a quality threshold
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find solutions in the top target ratio of the quality distribution
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Binary threshold marking on quality; no additional constraints specified

problem_instance.description: Arbitrarily large problem with normally distributed solution qualities
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Marked-solution ratio rho(T) taken as the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution at threshold T
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10,000 simulations over target ratios; success probability vs computational effort

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Use standard normal CDF to map threshold to marked-solution ratio
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute success probability curves and compare MAOA/RGAS to classical sampling

speedup_claims.conditions: small target-ratio limit; r = 64 in the large-problem simulation; repeated preparation and measurement of the maximally amplified state
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper derives the success-probability expression and the asymptotic speedup; the plotted comparison shows MAOA outperforming RGAS for smaller target ratios.

speedup_claims.factor: MAOA consistently outperforms RGAS for target ratios 1e-6 to 1e-10
speedup_claims.conditions: arbitrarily large normally distributed solution space; fixed r = 64; target ratios in {1e-6, 1e-7, 1e-8, 1e-9, 1e-10}
speedup_claims.caveats: No exact numeric speedup factor is given in the text; the result is shown in a figure.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(sqrt(N)) for unrestricted Grover adaptive search; MAOA uses r Grover rotations with per-sample cost O(2r+1)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N) for random sampling / exhaustive-style baseline
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Speedup over classical random sampling tends to 2r+1 in the small-target-ratio limit
